# THESIS

*The one-page form the track asks for: the claim, the evidence for it, the evidence against it, what would change our mind, and what could not be computed. Data to {{data_to}}; every figure is rendered from `data/processed/` by `make docs`. The full argument is in [`REPORT.md`](REPORT.md).*

## The claim

NEAR Intents' protocol revenue is real and has grown, but in its current form it does not support NEAR's value through supply: buybacks offset about a sixth of issuance, the recent jump was partly bought with an incentive and is already easing, and the market prices NEAR on something other than this revenue. Holding NEAR is a bet on Intents growing several times over at a higher take, not on scarcity.

## Evidence for

- **It is real.** Three independent indexers agree: NearBlocks, NEAR's BigQuery dataset (to the last digit on the NEAR the wallets received) and NEAR's own dashboard. Rebuilt from the chain, revenue matches DefiLlama within {{rev_gap}} ({{rev_rebuilt}} since the 2026-02-23 fee switch) and NEAR's own dashboard within {{wallets_gap}} on the NEAR its three revenue wallets received. ({{rev_rebuilt_exact}} vs {{rev_llama_exact}}; `make revenue`, `make official`)
- **In one line.** Of every $100 swapped through NEAR Intents ({{f100_from}} to {{f100_to}}), users pay {{f100_fees}} in fees, NEAR's wallets receive {{f100_near}}, and the network issues {{f100_issued}} of new NEAR: revenue covers {{f100_cover}} of issuance.
- **It is too small for the supply story.** Feb–Oct 2026: {{captured_feb_oct}} NEAR captured against {{issued_feb_oct}} issued, {{offset_rebuilt}} ({{offset_official}} on NEAR's own count). Supply still grows {{net_growth}} a year net. (`make supply`)
- **The gap is structural.** Supply stops growing only when market cap is below {{breakeven_now}} annual captured revenue ({{breakeven_cut}} after the approved HSP-029 cut); it is {{near_captured_mult}} (market cap on {{mcap_date}} ÷ wallet revenue {{r30_from}} to {{r30_to}}, annualised). Break-even needs about {{be_vol_now}} of daily volume at today's take, against about {{volume0}}. (`make montecarlo`)
- **2027 does not change it in the base case.** Median {{mc_base}} of 2027 issuance offset ({{mc_base_band}}), {{mc_base_p}} chance of a deflationary 2027; {{mc_cut}} with the issuance cut. The engine was too optimistic in its 2026 backtest. (`make montecarlo backtest`)
- **The jump was partly bought.** NEAR's take went from {{take_aug}} to {{take_oct}} bps between August and October; confidential swaps, which grew under the NEAR@3.33 airdrop, explain {{jump_fd}} to {{jump_levels}} of it. Drop 1 cost {{drop1_usd}}, {{drop1_over_uplift}} of the revenue uplift. (`make confidential`)
- **It is easing.** The fit missed its first unseen week ({{oos_actual}} vs {{oos_pred_fd}}–{{oos_pred}}); the take was {{take_last_week}} bps in the week of 2 November on three sources; confidential TVL is {{tvl_from_peak}} below its peak. (`make confidential official`)
- **NEAR does not own the customer.** On 1Click, integrators keep about {{oc_integrators_keep}} of the fee pool; SwapKit takes {{sk_fees}} of app fees and sends NEAR {{sk_near}} of its revenue. (`make swaps` outputs, to {{oc_to}})
- **Other flows dwarf the buyback.** US spot NEAR ETFs had taken in a net $80.5M by 5 November, ten times the {{rev_rebuilt}} NEAR has captured since the fee switch, and lost a net $5.74M in November to 12 November, against {{rev_nov01_11}} captured from 1 to 11 November (SoSoValue, via [ChainCatcher](https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2302233) and [AMBCrypto](https://ambcrypto.com/near-intents-fuels-2-7m-in-q4-buybacks-as-revenue-surges/); outside data, not rebuilt here). Price is set by flows several times larger than revenue.
- **The market agrees it is priced on something else.** Peers whose holders share revenue trade at a median {{peers_median}} holders revenue; NEAR at {{near_holders_mult}} on the same definition (DefiLlama holders revenue, last 30 days annualised, so slightly different from the {{near_captured_mult}} on the wallets); at the peer median its revenue supports about {{price_at_peer}} a NEAR, against {{price_now}}. Usage counts can mislead: from late October to early November transactions to `intents.near` changed {{bq_is_tx}} while captured revenue changed {{bq_is_rev}}, and {{bq_is_self_inc}} of the increase is the contract signing its own transactions (`make bigquery`). Usage does not lead the price: {{ll_sig}} of {{ll_tests}} lead-lag tests significant after Holm. (`make comps leadlag`)

## Evidence against

- **The take rate is a lever.** It doubled in two months (2.2 to 5.5 bps, month on month); at 8–15 bps with 2–4× today's volume, buybacks would cover issuance (sensitivity table in `make montecarlo`).
- **Confidential swaps do pay NEAR more**, in every method ({{premium_range}} bps against {{public_range}}). If a part of that use outlives the airdrop, the take stays well above its May–Aug level ({{take_mayaug}} bps).
- **The part NEAR controls held up in November.** On 1Click, NEAR's revenue from swaps without an integrator was {{noref_day_oct}} a day in late October and {{noref_day_nov}} in early November; the fall came from one integrator's burst ending (Trust Wallet). 
- **NEAR's own front-end is growing its share.** NEAR's dashboard shows capture by front-end fees rising from {{cap_fe_all}} of gross fees all-time to {{cap_fe_d30}} over the last 30 days: the flows NEAR controls are the ones that grew.
- **NEAR's own revenue series is higher.** It runs {{series_over_wallets}} above the wallets; if that revenue is real and retired, the offset is {{offset_official}} rather than {{offset_rebuilt}}. It does not change the order of magnitude.
- **Issuance is being cut.** HSP-029 passed with {{hsp_for}} of veNEAR cast; fully phased in, it lowers the break-even multiple's bar from {{breakeven_now}} to {{breakeven_cut}}.
- **It survived a freeze and an exploit, at the large integrators' expense.** 1Click stopped for {{ic_hours}} hours on 1 October, about {{ic_rev_lost}} of NEAR revenue, and users and NEAR's revenue stayed within their usual range in the two weeks after. But the 25 largest integrators' volume fell {{ic_top_vol}}, more than at any of {{ic_pn}} placebo dates, and only {{ic_back}} of the {{ic_cut}} that cut back had returned by November. (`make incident`)
- **The market pays for incentives, not for supply cuts.** Of seven NEAR events tested against a placebo distribution, only the NEAR@3.33 airdrop snapshot moved the price ({{ev_snap_px3}} against Bitcoin in three days); the issuance halving left it flat and HSP-029's approval was followed by {{ev_hsp_px3}}. (`make events`)
- **Users pay about {{sc_cost}} bps a swap on 1Click; NEAR keeps {{sc_near_share}} of it** ({{sc_int}} bps go to integrators, {{sc_rest}} to solvers and networks). (`make swap-cost`)
- **NEAR's revenue grows without more people signing NEAR transactions.** About {{sg_heavy_n}} heavy signers send {{sg_heavy_last}} of transactions; human-scale signers are {{sg_yoy}} on a year and lead nothing ({{sg_sig}} of {{sg_tests}} tests). (`make signers`)
- **The treasury's {{tr_moved}} NEAR moved this year was staked, not sold** ({{tr_x}}x the NEAR bought back since February): not selling pressure now, a stock its holders control. (`make treasury`)
- **Users do not visibly shop on fees.** Across {{el_n}} large 1Click integrators, the fee charged and the volume growth are unrelated (Spearman {{el_rho}}); the highest-fee ones grew most. The constraint on NEAR's take is the integrators' choice of router, not the users. (`make elasticity`)
- **The price implies far more revenue than exists.** At 15% and 3% growth it needs {{im_mid}}x today's captured revenue, or {{im_g5}} a year of growth for five years. (`make implied`)
- **Competition is not compressing the price yet.** In {{qr_rounds}} live quote rounds ({{qr_swaps}} identical swaps asked of 1Click, Relay, Across and LI.FI within the same minute, five corridors, about $1k and $20k), 1Click paid the user the most in {{qr_best_share}}, median {{qr_median}} from the best alternative, fees included: ahead on native BTC ({{qr_c_btc}}), level on L2 stablecoins and EVM swaps, behind on Ethereum to L2 ({{qr_c_l1l2}}) and Solana ({{qr_c_sol}}). NEAR's take is inside that price; where 1Click trails, the gap is about the size of that take. (`make quotes`)
- **Intents volume is growing** ({{yoy_vol}} over the last 30 days against a year earlier) while L1 activity falls ({{yoy_txns}} transactions): the part of NEAR that earns is the part that grows.

## What would change our mind

- **Toward the bull case:** the take holding above 5 bps through Q4 after the incentive (prediction P1 says it will not in early November; P5 says it stays above the May–Aug level); a revenue-sharing deal with SwapKit or another large integrator; an on-chain commitment by the front-end fund not to sell; daily volume several times higher at a stable take.
- **Toward a worse picture** (the pre-registered kill criteria, live on the dashboard): 30-day revenue below half its 180-day average (now {{kill1}}); buyback inflows stopping for 14 days while fees continue; one integrator above 60% of fees (triggered on 1Click, where SwapKit brings NEAR {{sk_near}} of its revenue).
- **Dated predictions** frozen on 2026-11-11 (`predictions/`), two resolving before judging.

## What could not be computed, and why

- **The fee on confidential swaps.** Not published, and not answered on three channels (NEAR Discord support, near.com support, the NearBuilders Telegram). Our hypothesis from the data (REPORT section 10): about **{{oq_bb_conf}} bps**, landing in the buyback multisig (interval {{oq_bb_band}}; {{oq_bb_fd}} on week-to-week changes), in line with NEAR's Dune fee table (7.4).
- **Where NEAR's extra {{series_over_wallets}} of reported revenue goes.** Not answered either. Our hypothesis (REPORT section 10): mostly **quote-improvement revenue** ({{oq_qi_share}} of what NEAR reports), which does not reach the three wallets; without it the series is within {{oq_gap_ytd_ex}} of the wallets this year and {{oq_gap_d30_ex}} over the last 30 days.
- **Confidential swaps by integrator or asset.** The Explorer API shows only 1Click (public) swaps; Dune's asset tables could not be read consistently (log 26).
- **Whether NEAR@3.33 caused the growth.** The timing fits; there is no control group, and near.com shipped other products over the same months.
